name: US EPA CompTox / CTX APIs
notes: EPA CTX data are open for commercial and non-commercial use. An individual API key is required for limited-access APIs. Preserve original source/context because the Dashboard aggregates data from many sources. Live-tested 2026-09-23 (app/services/epa_comptox.py): the Hazard API's ToxValDB by-dtxsid endpoint returned zero humanEco=='eco' records across seven real chemicals (1,832 total records, all human-health/mammalian) -- it is wired up and correctly filters for eco records, but should not be relied on for aquatic/avian ecotoxicity coverage today; epa_ecotox's local bulk import remains comprehensive for that.

name: PubChem PUG REST + PUG View
notes: PUG REST resolves identifiers and computed properties. PUG View supplies third-party annotations and attribution. Keep requests below PubChem's published service limits.

name: Europe PMC
notes: Search abstracts and metadata for all indexed literature. Numeric candidate extraction from OA full text is supported only for the Open Access subset; article-specific licence terms remain attached to the candidate.

name: EFSA OpenFoodTox 3.0
notes: OpenFoodTox 3.0 includes structured environmental fate/behaviour, physicochemical and ecotoxicology study results. EnviroChem stages official Excel/IUCLID exports rather than scraping the site.

name: US EPA ECOTOX Knowledgebase
notes: Curated ecotoxicity records from peer-reviewed literature. Live-searchable once a reviewer has run scripts/import_ecotox.py against a fresh bulk download -- app/services/ecotox_local.py returns an explicit 'not_imported' status, not a silent empty result, when that hasn't been done yet. Current scope: aquatic-medium LC50/EC50/NOEC/EC10 only (~211k records / ~5,300 chemicals as of the 2026-09-15 EPA release); full terrestrial/other-endpoint coverage is not imported.

name: EcoDrug+
owner: University of Helsinki / University of Exeter
notes: Useful for effects/mechanism and cross-species target conservation rather than environmental degradation kinetics.

name: PHARMS-UBA — Pharmaceuticals in the Environment
notes: Monitoring/MEC evidence across many matrices; do not use as a degradation-kinetics database.

name: NORMAN Ecotoxicology Database
notes: Useful for experimental endpoints and expert-selected Lowest PNECs. Lowest PNECs are prioritisation values and still require regulatory-context review.

name: OECD eChemPortal
notes: Use to locate authoritative source datasets. Rights and reliability remain those of each underlying data owner.

name: ECHA CHEM
notes: Up-to-date REACH registration data are now in ECHA CHEM. Some information may belong to third parties; bulk commercial reuse is not enabled in EnviroChem without a rights review.

name: AERU Veterinary Substances Database (VSDB)
notes: Excellent veterinary fate source, including manure DT50 where available. Some human APIs appear where they also have veterinary relevance, but VSDB is not a comprehensive human-pharmaceutical database. Commercial copying/integration requires a licence.

name: AERU Pesticide Properties Database (PPDB)
notes: Strong pesticide fate/ecotox source. EnviroChem does not scrape or redistribute PPDB data; licensed offline exports can be connected once commercial rights are obtained.

name: PREMIER Digital Assessment System
owner: IMI2 PREMIER consortium / Mario Negri Institute
notes: High-value human-pharmaceutical source. Commercial use, including marketing-authorisation use, is not enabled unless the controlling data party has granted a formal letter of access. EnviroChem therefore supports permission-gated export/import rather than covert scraping.

name: Sci-Bot
notes: The service publicly identifies itself as powered by Sci-Hub. EnviroChem does not use it. Europe PMC/Open Access APIs are the lawful literature-mining route.

name: FASS Environmental Information for Pharmaceuticals
owner: LIF / Swedish pharmaceutical information system; environmental data supplied by marketing-authorisation holders
notes: High-value human-pharmaceutical environmental summaries. Individual product pages can expose OECD study results including ready/inherent biodegradation, water-sediment DT50, hydrolysis, Koc/logD and ecotoxicity. EnviroChem links out but does not scrape or republish FASS content until reuse terms are confirmed.

name: Region Stockholm — Pharmaceuticals and Environment
notes: Human-pharmaceutical environmental hazard/risk decision support covering persistence, bioaccumulation and toxicity, with contextual information such as WWTP removal/occurrence where available. Registered as a linkout pending a formal reuse/API review.

name: Japan NIHS — Human Pharmaceutical ERA Databases
notes: NIHS publishes a human-pharmaceutical ecotoxicity Excel database and a separate environmental-fate database. The NIHS copyright policy states that, unless specifically noted otherwise, site content can be used under Japan's Public Data License 1.0 with attribution. EnviroChem registers the downloads for a verified local importer rather than silently scraping them.

name: US EPA Exposure Factors Handbook
notes: Values are never inserted silently. Store chapter/table, population or life stage, statistic, edition/update and access date with each selected parameter.

name: US EPA ChemSTEER
notes: EnviroChem prepares and reviews versioned manifests and outputs. The executable is not bundled, modified or represented as EnviroChem intellectual property.

name: US EPA Consumer Exposure Model
notes: EnviroChem stores category, route, population, life-stage and model choices with reviewed imported output; it does not bundle or modify CEM.

name: US EPA E-FAST 2014
notes: Every result remains labelled 2014/legacy with executable and scenario provenance. EnviroChem does not modify or redistribute E-FAST.

name: enviPath / EAWAG-BBD and PPS
notes: The open-source client licence does not automatically grant commercial redistribution rights to hosted records or PPS content. Keep this as a collaboration/permission-gated provider.

name: KEGG Xenobiotics Biodegradation and Metabolism
notes: Do not ingest or redistribute KEGG pathway data in the paid product without an appropriate commercial licence. API availability does not remove that requirement.

name: PEPPER soil DT50 model (Eawag/UZH) via FateIntel provider
notes: Probabilistic Gaussian-process model (Hafner et al., ES&T 2026) trained on EAWAG-SOIL (Latino et al., 2017). Returns the measured EAWAG-SOIL mean when the compound is in the training set, otherwise a labelled prediction with confidence and applicability domain. Peer-reviewed, moderate performance, but no QMRF and not an OECD-accepted QSAR; trained on EU pesticides and transformation products, so pharmaceuticals, industrial chemicals and PFAS are sparse. Runs only in local/test evaluation until an operator confirms the training-data licence.

name: OASIS soil biodegradation DT50 (QSAR Toolbox, LMC)
owner: Laboratory of Mathematical Chemistry (LMC), Bourgas; OASIS-LMC / QSAR Toolbox
notes: 218 real measured 'Biodegradation in soil' records from the QSAR Toolbox 4.9 storehouse (OASIS-LMC), matched by exact structure. A real measured DT50, not a prediction -- used ahead of PEPPER and BIOWIN4 in the soil-fate ladder when it exists for the exact structure. Runs only in local/test evaluation until an operator confirms the QSAR Toolbox data licence.

name: NITE ready-biodegradability / mineralization data (QSAR Toolbox, METI Japan)
owner: National Institute of Technology and Evaluation (NITE), Japan (METI/CSCL); distributed via QSAR Toolbox
notes: 1,373 real measured ready-biodegradability screening records (percent ThOD/ThCO2 via O2 consumption, OECD TG 301/302), matched by exact structure. A ready-biodegradability screening percentage, not a soil or water DT50 -- shown as context (mineralization + pass/fail), never used to derive kinetics. Pass/fail classification (60% ThOD threshold) confirmed against OECD Test Guideline 301 primary text (1992, para. 10, Table 1); applies to 301C-labelled records only -- 301D is indicative-only, 302C is a different (inherent, not ready) endpoint and is not classified. Runs only in local/test evaluation until an operator confirms the QSAR Toolbox data licence.
